amaryllis-fox-kennedy.title: Amaryllis Fox Kennedy
amaryllis-fox-kennedy.summary: Former CIA non-official-cover officer who worked under commercial cover as an international art consultant, later a Trump campaign manager and nominee for deputy CIA director. Per John Kiriakou, Senator Tom Cotton threatened to filibuster her appointment; the president responded by naming her deputy national security adviser instead — a job Kiriakou considers more powerful, since the CIA director reports to the national security adviser.
dyk: ...that when Senator Tom Cotton threatened to filibuster Amaryllis Fox Kennedy's appointment as deputy [CIA](/wiki/cia) director, she was instead named deputy national security adviser — a job [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) calls *"way more important,"* because the CIA director reports to the national security adviser?

...that [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) says Amaryllis Fox Kennedy served under [non-official cover](/wiki/aldrich-ames) as an international art consultant — a field he elsewhere identifies, on a Treasury contact's authority, as one of the last three channels through which [money can still be laundered](/wiki/kiriakou-moneylaundering-tip)?
amaryllis-fox-kennedy.body:
**Amaryllis Fox Kennedy** is a former [CIA](/wiki/cia) officer whom [John Kiriakou](/wiki/john-kiriakou) identifies as having served under non-official cover. Her commercial cover, he says he is told, was as an international art consultant — a line of work he notes carries a great deal of money, a great deal of hidden money, and a great deal of money laundering, which is what made it serviceable.<Cite t="1:56:17" /><Cite t="1:58:20" />

## The blocked nomination

Kiriakou says she was to have been deputy director of the CIA, and that Senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas — whom he characterises as a statist and a neoconservative — refused. His reading of the motive is personal rather than substantive: Cotton had wanted to be CIA director himself, was passed over for [Mike Pompeo](/wiki/mike-pompeo) in Trump's first term, and resented the appearance of an upstart, married to Robert F. Kennedy's son and lately the campaign manager, taking a job he thought should have been his.<Cite t="1:58:20" /><Cite t="1:58:53" />

Cotton sent word to the White House that he would filibuster the appointment. Kiriakou's assessment of what happened next is that the president outmanoeuvred him: *"the president did something that was just so smart — he named her deputy national security adviser, which is a way more important job, because the CIA director reports to the national security adviser."*<Cite t="1:59:27" />

Kiriakou notes that the counterterrorism portfolio within that office was not hers, being held by [Sebastian Gorka](/wiki/sebastian-gorka), with whom Kiriakou has both a personal and a professional quarrel.<Cite t="1:59:27" /><Cite t="1:59:57" />
